title: To Infinity and Beyond: ThunderKittens Now on NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72!
gist: Together AI's kernels team got early access to NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 and found that existing Blackwell GEMM kernels hit only 42.1 percent (NVFP4) and 44.4 percent (FP8) of roofline because the tensor cores now consume operands twice as fast than the memory path can feed them; after exploiting doubled-K MMAs, 576-column tensor memory, 328 KiB shared memory, B-side collectors and early A release they reached over 22 PFLOPS, competitive with cuBLAS. The practical lesson is that Rubin's ~4x paper FLOPS gain is unreachable without a software rewrite, so realized speedups will lag hardware announcements.

themes.theme: Vera Rubin versus Blackwell silicon deltas

insights.claim: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 delivers 35 PFLOPS per GPU of NVFP4 tensor core throughput versus 9 PFLOPS on HGX B200, 17.5 versus 4.5 PFLOPS for FP8, and 4 versus 2.25 PFLOPS for FP16/BF16 — roughly a 4x jump for low precision but under 2x for half precision.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: The generational gain is concentrated in 4-bit formats, so the headline speedup only materializes for workloads that have already migrated to NVFP4.
insights.locator: What's new with the NVIDIA Vera Rubin Platform?

insights.claim: Vera Rubin lifts memory bandwidth to 22 TB/s per GPU from 8 TB/s on B200 and SM count to 224 from 148, while peak power rises to 2300W per GPU from 1000W.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: A 2.3x jump in per-GPU power draw is the single most consequential number for datacenter cooling, power contracts and utility demand forecasts.
insights.locator: NVIDIA HGX B200NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72

insights.claim: Bandwidth grew 2.75x while NVFP4 compute grew 3.9x, meaning the compute-to-bandwidth ratio worsened generation over generation and kernels must extract more on-chip data reuse to stay fed.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: Widening compute-to-memory imbalance is the structural reason memory-centric accelerators and HBM suppliers keep gaining leverage.
insights.quote: The core issue we find is that while Rubin enables tensor cores to consume operands twice as fast, our old Blackwell kernel does not feed them fast enough.
insights.locator: The rest of this post is in two parts

insights.claim: Running existing Blackwell kernels unmodified on Vera Rubin achieved only about 42.1 percent of roofline for NVFP4 and 44.4 percent for FP8 — code portability is preserved but performance is not.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: Buyers upgrading to new silicon capture only ~40 percent of the theoretical gain until kernels are rewritten — a real lag between hardware shipment and effective capacity.
insights.locator: As Rubin preserves the Blackwell programming model

insights.claim: Blackwell's 32-byte K-step encoding has an ISA ceiling of roughly 16.8 PFLOPs on Vera Rubin, and the unmodified Blackwell NVFP4 GEMM already hit 14.7 PFLOPs — 88 percent of that ceiling — so further gains required adopting the new 64-byte K step, not better tuning.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: Instruction-set ceilings, not tuning effort, gate performance — an argument that CUDA-generation lock-in is deepening rather than easing.

insights.claim: Simply flipping on the wider 64-byte K encoding in the existing kernel produced only marginal improvement rather than the expected 2x, because the wider MMA doubles operand consumption speed without improving operand supply.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: Vendor feature checklists mislead: new instructions deliver nothing without co-designed data movement, which is why kernel expertise is a scarce and valuable input.
insights.locator: However, simply flipping on the wider encoding

insights.claim: After integrating the new features, the NVFP4 kernel reached over 22 PFLOPS and became competitive with cuBLAS and CuTE DSL, roughly a 1.5x gain over the 14.7 PFLOPs starting point.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: An open kernel library matching NVIDIA's own cuBLAS narrows a key part of the CUDA moat and supports third-party framework independence.
insights.locator: Then, we slowly integrate these features

insights.claim: All measurements were made with NVIDIA CUDA 13.4 on a Qualification Sample GPU, with the authors expecting baseline performance to improve further as Vera Rubin software releases mature.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: Pre-production silicon and immature software mean early Rubin benchmarks understate shipping performance — discount early competitive comparisons.

themes.theme: New Rubin ISA features that move performance

insights.claim: A tcgen05.mma step consumes 32 bytes along K on Blackwell but can consume 64 bytes on Vera Rubin while taking the same number of cycles, letting twice as much work be packed into the same instruction window.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: The core Rubin throughput gain comes from instruction-window density, which only helps kernels rewritten to keep the pipe full.
insights.locator: 1. Tensor cores take twice the K

insights.claim: Tensor memory grows from a 128 lane by 512 column space on Blackwell to 576 columns on Vera Rubin, adding 32 KiB, but the extra columns are reachable only through the PTX 9.4 .exclusive qualifier that requires a single live tensor memory allocation per SM.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: Capability gated behind exclusivity constraints means real-world gains depend on whether a workload can monopolize an SM.

insights.claim: Vera Rubin introduces an oversized shared memory mode that dynamically raises shared memory from the 228 KiB available on Hopper and Blackwell to 328 KiB, enabled by a host-side function attribute.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: A 44 percent larger on-chip scratchpad is what makes deeper software pipelines — and therefore the realized speedup — possible.

insights.claim: Blackwell's collector buffer, a small MMA staging buffer that could latch an A tile, is extended on Vera Rubin to the B tile, so over a 2x2 block collecting on both sides cuts four MMAs from eight operand reads down to five.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: Hardware-level operand reuse is the mechanism by which NVIDIA keeps compute scaling ahead of memory — and it requires explicit kernel annotation to access.

insights.claim: Collector labels FILL, USE, LASTUSE and DISCARD are permission qualifiers for reuse rather than guarantees, meaning the tensor core may still reload a matrix even when permitted to reuse it.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: Non-deterministic hardware behavior means measured speedups from these features will vary by workload — treat vendor feature claims as upper bounds.
insights.quote: These labels are permission qualifiers for reuse, not guarantees.

insights.claim: PTX 9.4 adds tcgen05.commit.sync_restrict::shared::read::mma::a, which fires the barrier as soon as an MMA has finished reading its A operand out of shared memory rather than waiting for the MMA to complete, letting the TMA loader start the next stage earlier.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: Finer-grained synchronization primitives are where the remaining double-digit percentage gains live on modern GPUs.

insights.claim: Deepening the shared-memory pipeline drove the largest single gain on the NVFP4 16k square GEMM: 3 stages at 202 KiB delivered 17,054 TFLOPS, 4 stages at 258 KiB delivered 20,595 TFLOPS, and 5 stages at 314 KiB delivered 22,239 TFLOPS.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: A 30 percent throughput swing from pipeline depth alone shows how much realized GPU value depends on software, not silicon.

insights.claim: FP8 scaling behaved differently from NVFP4: 4 stages gave 10,895 TFLOPS, 5 stages peaked at 11,995 TFLOPS, and 6 stages regressed to 11,288 TFLOPS, showing pipeline depth has an optimum rather than monotonic returns.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: Per-precision tuning curves differ, so a single optimized configuration cannot serve a mixed-precision fleet — more engineering cost per deployment.

insights.claim: Early A release delivered 13.5 percent and 22.1 percent speedups on 64k and 128k square NVFP4 GEMMs respectively, but gave nothing at smaller sizes where A tiles never leave L2 and reads are already fast enough.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: Optimizations pay off only at very large matrix sizes, meaning benchmark-size choice can swing reported generational gains substantially.

insights.claim: The B-side collector was measured at only 1 to 3 percent improvement and L2 EVICT_LAST eviction hints helped by a few tenths of a percent, so the headline features contributed far less than pipeline depth and tiling changes.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: Marquee architectural features can be near-noise in practice — useful skepticism when a vendor's spec sheet drives a purchase thesis.

insights.claim: Moving from a 1x1 to a 2x1 CTA pair tiling format lets two output accumulators differing only in M share the same B chunk, halving B operand traffic for the same M512xN256 output coverage.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: Tiling geometry, a pure software choice, halves memory traffic — the cheapest lever available when bandwidth is the constraint.

insights.claim: The 2x1 tiling was not practical on Blackwell because tensor memory capped at 256 KiB meant two M256xN256 accumulators consumed all 512 columns, leaving no room for block-scaled MMA A and B scales; Vera Rubin's extra 64 columns removed that constraint.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: A seemingly minor 64-column capacity increase unlocked an entire algorithmic strategy — small architectural changes can have outsized software consequences.
insights.locator: This 2x1 tiling format was not easily achievable

insights.claim: Kernel configuration must vary with workload shape: the original 1x1 tile format remained most performant for smaller square workloads while larger shapes used 2x1 tiling with tuned cluster sizes of 2, 4 or 8 CTAs, plus permuted tile rasterization order for memory locality.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: No single optimal kernel exists across shapes, so serving heterogeneous model workloads at peak efficiency requires ongoing kernel engineering headcount.

insights.claim: Enabling early A release required decoupling A and B tiles from a shared ring and single commit into separate rings with their own arrived/finished barrier pairs, a non-trivial restructuring of standard GEMM pipeline logic.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: The engineering cost of each new instruction is high, favoring a small number of well-resourced kernel teams and the libraries they publish.
insights.locator: In order to utilize this instruction

themes.theme: Blackwell programming model as the baseline

insights.claim: Blackwell fundamentally changed the GEMM programming model: Hopper's wgmma instruction was issued collectively by a warpgroup while Blackwell's tcgen05 is issued by a single thread, the accumulator moved from registers into tensor memory, operands are read directly from shared memory, and a single MMA can span two CTAs across two SMs.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: Rubin preserving this model means the Blackwell-era software investment carries forward — reducing switching friction and reinforcing NVIDIA's compounding software advantage.
insights.locator: Starting Point: An NVIDIA HGX B200 GEMM

insights.claim: Competitive Blackwell GEMMs relied on three patterns: threadblock clusters where CTA pairs share operands via TMA multicast to halve HBM traffic, warp specialization into loader/MMA/consumer roles, and persistent kernels that stream one tile's inputs while the previous tile's outputs drain.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: These three patterns are the reusable template for extracting peak throughput on any modern tensor-core GPU.
insights.locator: To reach competitive performance on Blackwell

insights.claim: Together AI's kernels and performance teams are actively hiring and publicly soliciting contacts, with further work teased on LUT GEMMs, hardware-native megakernels and new engine optimizations.
insights.speaker: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
insights.so_what: Aggressive hiring for low-level kernel talent signals where neoclouds believe their remaining cost advantage comes from.

source_meta.author: Dylan Lim, Xinyi Li, Sonny Li, Peter Wu, Dan Fu, Simran Arora
